summary: The v40 lamp mismatch came from the hero-swallow path in mhitu.c:gulpmu calling apply.c:snuff_lit while JavaScript left the carried lamp lit. JavaScript now implements the complete snuff_lit helper and wires all six direct C caller paths: splash_lit, gulpmu, gulpmm, gulpum, use_container, and litroom (with the splash helper used by both hero and monster water-damage branches). An independent C-first purple-worm recording reaches gulpmu with a lit oil lamp and matches through ‘Your lamp goes out!’ The admitted v40 replay now shows that lamp transition correctly; its later obj_resists(zap.c:1469) RNG and HP mismatch remains a separate source boundary.

source.branch: When obj->lamplit is false, snuff_lit returns FALSE. For a lit oil lamp, magic lamp, brass lantern, or potion of oil, it checks cansee at OBJ_MINVENT coordinates and otherwise checks !Blind, prints Yname2(obj) plus otense(obj, "go") when visible, calls end_burn(obj, TRUE), and returns TRUE. Other lit objects go through snuff_candle; its result is returned when it extinguishes a candle or candelabrum, otherwise snuff_lit returns FALSE.
callers: apply.c:splash_lit calls snuff_lit(obj) at 1564; JavaScript routes the hero water-splash branch through trap_effects.js:splash_hero_light and the monster branch through apply_splash_lit.js:splash_monster_light.
mhitu.c:gulpmu calls snuff_lit for each hero inventory object after the swallowed transition at 1400; JavaScript calls it from js/mhitu.js:gulpmu.
mhitm.c:gulpmm calls snuff_lit for defender inventory objects at 870; JavaScript calls it from js/mhitm.js:gulpmm.
uhitm.c:gulpum calls snuff_lit for monster inventory objects at 4986; JavaScript calls it from js/uhitm.js:gulpum.
pickup.c:use_container calls snuff_lit after removing a burning object from inventory at 2627; JavaScript calls it from js/pickup.js:in_container.
read.c:litroom calls snuff_lit for each carried non-artifact light while darkening the area at 2517; JavaScript calls it from js/read.js:litroom.
dependencies: apply.c:snuff_candle is already implemented in js/apply_splash_lit.js and is called for candle and candelabrum objects.
timeout.c:end_burn is already implemented in js/timeout.js; snuff_lit discards its return value.

The accepted v40 evaluation had 76/79 screens, 2812/2825 RNG calls, and 79/79 cursors; its first screen mismatch showed C “Y” and JS “T” at the gulp lamp transition.

Reviewed the complete upstream apply.c:snuff_lit definition at lines 1493-1514, including its visibility split, Yname2/otense message order, end_burn state update, candle delegation, and FALSE return. Read all seven direct call sites and their JavaScript paths listed under source.callers.

Before the fix, js/mhitu.js: gulpmu recorded note_unported("light.c snuff_lit"); js/apply_splash_lit.js only had snuff_monster_light, which required OBJ_MINVENT and could not handle gulpmu’s OBJ_INVENT objects. The same placeholder existed at the gulpmm, gulpum, use_container, and litroom callsites.

js/apply_splash_lit.js now exports snuff_lit, which reproduces the whole apply.c helper and delegates the candle branch to snuff_candle. The gulp, container, light-scroll, and splash callers use that shared helper in C source order; trap_effects.js no longer duplicates a private lamp-snuff branch.

The independent recipe recipes/mhitu.c/b218-gulpmu-lit-oil-lamp-independent.session.json was freshly recorded and matched with node scripts/diff-fresh.mjs: 44/44 screens, 2776/2776 RNG calls, and 44/44 cursors. Its C recording records mattacku -> gulpmu at step 42, the gulp message, then gulpmu’s inventory loop and “Your lamp goes out!” at step 43. replay.traceCorrection: The step-75 leash page is produced by mhitu.c:gulpmu calling apply.c:unleash_all; apply.c:check_leash remains unreached by this input path.

sourceTrace.branch: On the first swallow, gulpmu emits the swallow message, handles release from a trap, then counts attached leashes. When at least one exists it prints “The leash snaps loose.” and calls unleash_all(), which clears every inventory leashmon and every monster mleashed flag. This page is not produced by apply.c:check_leash.
callers: mhitu.c:gulpmu calls number_leashed() and unleash_all() at lines 1349–1355 after the swallow transition.
apply.c:unleash_all() (746–754) clears leashmon for every inventory leash, then mleashed for every monster in fmon.
Other C call sites are trap.c (5103), shk.c (2745), and bones.c (435); they are outside this recorded gulp path.
jsGaps: js/mhitu.js:gulpmu reproduces the count and message but replaces the state transition with note_unported('apply.c unleash_all') at lines 2315–2320.
There is no canonical js/apply.js:unleash_all implementation yet.
apply.c:check_leash has no call in mhitu.c:gulpmu. Its direct C callers are hack.c:domove_core, trap.c:move_into_trap, and allmain.c:moveloop_core; none produces this gulp page.
sourceTrace.evidence: In the admitted recording, step 74 (key “.”) reaches the purple-worm gulp and records “The purple worm swallows you whole!--More--”. Step 75 (key space) acknowledges the pending page and displays “The leash snaps loose.--More--” with no RNG calls. The source order places the leash message and unleash_all call in gulpmu. JS currently prints the same page but leaves the pet attached, which explains why the next turn enters a different dog_move path. The previous check_leash attribution was incorrect.
